coreModelUse: Every finding gets a name and a reason, and the proof section insists on both sides before calling anything closed.

sections.why: Name the real task: audit your own router and close the openings nobody chose.

rejected.why: A paragraph opening buries the one-task framing the audit depends on.

sections.why: Activate the inventory, baseline and translation-versus-permission model the audit reuses.

rejected.why: Nothing to score yet; a right/wrong check this early punishes inventory recall instead of activating it.

sections.why: Demonstrate the whole job on one example router: each finding walked to keep, close or unknown.

rejected.why: The worked example is parallel verdicts on one router, not a procedure to perform in order.

sections.why: Show how each verdict was reached: own records first, then the authorized owner; unfamiliar stays unknown.

rejected.why: The verdict method is the lesson itself; a side callout demotes it to optional.

sections.why: The apply sequence on the reader's own router, in order, one change at a time.

rejected.why: One recorded change at a time is ordered; a checklist implies any order.

sections.why: The reader records their own findings and verdicts; empty fields reset and are not evidence.

rejected.why: The reader's own findings have no single right answer to score.

sections.why: Integrate: inside view and outside attempt are separate proofs; one alone does not close the question.

rejected.why: Inside proof and outside proof need parallel columns; prose blurs which side failed.

sections.why: Check the model: a failed outside attempt with a live LAN listener means the boundary is closed, not the service.

rejected.why: The point is reasoning to one verdict with explanation, not an unscored pick.

sections.why: Consent and recovery: own router, owner's okay, and recorded changes can be re-added by name.

rejected.why: Consent and recovery are bounded cautions beside the task, not a main argument.

sections.why: UPnP and home-router guidance grounds the audit.

rejected.why: Links in prose hide the primary UPnP and router guidance the audit leans on.

sections.why: Point at the lab boundary page the closed openings make safe to build.

rejected.why: A bare rule line drops the reader with no hand-off to the lab boundary page.
The proof is two checks, not a packet path; the comparison carries it.
Router admin pages differ by vendor; invented commands would teach a UI nobody has.
